title: Airbnb earnings analysis: questions answered and next catalysts
detail:
Airbnb earnings analysis: questions answered and next catalysts
Investing.com
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:32 AM MST 3 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Airbnb Inc (ABNB) reported Q3 2026 results on Nov 5 after the close. The company beat on every line, and the market responded. The stock is at $190.96 (+12.24%) as of Nov 6, 12:50 PM EST, close to its 52-week high of $193.45.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Questions Answered

Question

	

Answer

	

Evidence




Is growth really reaccelerating?

	

Yes

	

Revenue $4.87B vs $4.75B est, up 19% YoY, the fastest in over three years




Is it just a pricing effect?

	

Mostly not

	

Nights & Seats Booked rose 16% to 155M, from about 10% in Q2. Canaccord estimates about 13% excluding a 3-point lift from Reserve Now, Pay Later.




Is it broad-based?

	

Yes

	

All major regions accelerated, and first-time bookers hit their strongest pace in several years (Jefferies).




Can profitability hold?

	

Yes

	

EBITDA was $2.51B at a 52% margin. FY2026 margin guidance was lifted to about 36%.




Is the industry weakness hitting Airbnb?

	

Not so far

	

Booking Holdings, Expedia and TripAdvisor flagged higher airfares and European unrest. Airbnb guided above the Street.

EPS was $3.16 vs $2.85 est (+10.9%). Gross booking value rose 21% to $27.7B. FY2026 revenue growth guidance moved to "high teens" from "at least mid-teens". That is the third consecutive raise.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Earnings history shows a clear turn. EPS missed in Q4 2025 (-15%) and Q1 2026 (-16%). Then it beat in Q2 (+8.7%, stock +16.8%) and Q3.

Caveats Still Open

Guidance assumes calm. It excludes any persistent hit from unrest in France or the Middle East conflict.

Q4 growth moderates. Nights Booked growth faces tougher comparisons, and EBITDA margin dips slightly YoY as marketing spend shifts into Q4.

Valuation is rich. Cantor (Neutral, $180 target) cites about 27x FY2027 P/E. InvestingPro shows a trailing P/E of 38.5. Evercore's comparison is 14x for Booking Holdings and 11x for Expedia.

The stock has already run. It is +58.4% over 1 year and +19% over 1 month (as of Nov 6).

Part of the boost is mechanical. Reserve Now, Pay Later expansion contributed to the Nights Booked acceleration.

Next Catalysts

Q4 guidance delivery. Revenue guidance is $3.22B–$3.28B vs the $3.16B Street estimate. Q4 results are expected around Feb 16, 2027 (tentative). Consensus is EPS $0.85 and revenue $3.16B, and it will likely rise.

$12B buyback. The new authorization compares with $12.6B of cash and short-term investments at Sep 30. It gives a floor of support.

AI Travel Agent. Launch is planned for the first half of 2027, with broader "agentic experiences" next year. Mizuho calls ABNB its top internet pick and sets a $245 target, the Street high.

Hotels and services. Hotels are growing "markedly faster" than the core rental business but remain a single-digit share of revenue. There is also a new American Express partnership and car rentals.

Estimate revisions. Consensus EPS is $5.31 for FY2026 and $6.26 for FY2027. Revisions over 90 days are only +1.6%, so there is room to catch up.

Macro risks. Airfares and European unrest could undermine the "no material impact" assumption.

title: Airbnb Jumps 11% After Hours on Its Fastest Growth in More Than 3 Years
detail:
Airbnb Jumps 11% After Hours on Its Fastest Growth in More Than 3 Years
Omor Ibne Ehsan
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 10:57 AM MST 4 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

Airbnb stock surged 11% after hours as third-quarter revenue grew 19%, beating estimates and prompting a raised full-year outlook.

Skeptics note currency and Reserve Now, Pay Later flatter results: revenue excluding currency rose 16%, and CFO Ellie Mertz put nights growth near 13% without the feature.

Airbnb bought back $700 million of stock in Q3 and approved a new $12 billion buyback program.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) shares closed lower in regular trading on November 5, 2026, down 3.54% at $170.13. A few hours later, they traded at $188.84 after hours. That 11.00% jump put the stock close to its 52-week high of $193.45 and far above its 52-week low of $110.81.

stockcam / iStock Unreleased via Getty Images

The move came after Airbnb reported third-quarter revenue of $4.869 billion, up 19%, and raised its full-year outlook. Only weeks earlier, investors had worried that AI agents would book travel directly and leave platforms out of the transaction. Investors are considering whether this growth will last, or whether a payment-timing feature and currency are making it look better than it is.

ABNB Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Revenue Reaccelerated and Beat Estimates

On the call, Chief Executive Brian Chesky said: "Q3 was our fastest revenue growth in more than three years." Revenue came in above the $4.75 billion consensus, and diluted EPS of $3.16 exceeded the $2.85 estimate.

Gross booking value, meaning the total dollar value of bookings, rose 21% to $27.7 billion. Because bookings made now turn into revenue later, faster booking growth sets up future quarters.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 22% to $2.509 billion, a 52% margin. Free cash flow was $1.426 billion.

How Much of the Growth Is Real

The bear case rests on two points. First, excluding currency, revenue grew 16%. Second, nights and seats booked rose 16%, but CFO Ellie Mertz said that figure was about 13% once you remove the lift from Reserve Now, Pay Later.

title: Airbnb Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Raised Outlook
detail:
Airbnb Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Raised Outlook
Zacks Equity Research
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:33 AM MST 4 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Airbnb, Inc. ABNB emphasized accelerating bookings, faster product innovation and improving operating efficiency during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management raised its full-year outlook as momentum strengthened across established and expansion markets.

CEO Brian Chesky attributed the acceleration to years of platform improvements, pricing initiatives and organizational changes. The company is also expanding into hotels, services and AI-powered travel planning to support longer-term growth.

The company reported third-quarter revenues of $4.87 billion, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.75 billion. Earnings per share of $3.16 surpassed the consensus estimate of $2.86. Management nevertheless flagged developments in Europe and the Middle East as areas requiring continued monitoring.

Airbnb, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Airbnb, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Airbnb, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Airbnb, Inc. Quote

ABNB Raises Full-Year Outlook as Demand Strengthens

Chief financial officer Ellie Mertz raised the company's full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to the high teens from the previous expectation of at least mid-teens growth.

Airbnb also increased its adjusted EBITDA margin forecast to approximately 36% from at least 35.5%. For the fourth quarter, management projected revenues to be between $3.22 billion and $3.28 billion, representing 16% to 18% year-over-year growth.

Airbnb Sees Pricing and Flexible Payments Driving Bookings

Chesky highlighted pricing improvements as an important opportunity for increasing bookings and host earnings. During the analyst Q&A, a Bernstein analyst questioned early adoption of dynamic pricing.

Chesky described host adoption as encouraging, emphasizing that more competitive nightly rates could improve occupancy while increasing overall host earnings. He characterized the initiative as an early-stage opportunity.

Mertz explained that Reserve Now, Pay Later contributed approximately three percentage points to third-quarter Nights and Seats Booked growth of 16%. However, cancellation rates increased to approximately 19% from 16% a year earlier, and management expects the initiative's net booking contribution to moderate sequentially in the fourth quarter.

ABNB Expands AI Capabilities Across Travel Services

Chesky outlined plans to introduce Airbnb's specialized AI travel agent during the first half of 2027. The platform will integrate maps, photographs, comparisons and itineraries into a customized travel-planning interface.

Responding to questions from Mizuho and Wells Fargo analysts, Chesky explained that the company intends to integrate external travel providers and eventually enable broader travel bookings directly through Airbnb.
